reglementation.titre: Low voltage safety file and CE
reglementation.acte: Directive 2014/35/EU (low voltage)
reglementation.autorite: European Parliament and Council of the European Union; enforced by national market surveillance authorities
reglementation.citation: Where compliance of electrical equipment with the safety objectives referred to in Article 3 and set out in Annex I has been demonstrated by the conformity assessment procedure referred to in the first subparagraph, manufacturers shall draw up an EU declaration of conformity and affix the CE marking.
reglementation.exigence: Once the conformity assessment has shown compliance with the safety objectives, the manufacturer must draw up an EU declaration of conformity and affix the CE marking.
reglementation.note: Article 6(2), first subparagraph: the manufacturer draws up the technical documentation of Annex III and carries out the conformity assessment. Scope read in Article 1: equipment rated between 50 and 1 000 V AC and between 75 and 1 500 V DC. The charger (input 100-240 V AC) is inside these limits. The laptop input is 20 V DC, below the 75 V DC limit, so its safety is handled through the radio equipment directive (see eu-red-exigences). Article 6(3): documentation and declaration kept 10 years. Article 8: the importer checks all this before placing on the market.

reglementation.titre: EMC conformity assessment and CE
reglementation.acte: Directive 2014/30/EU (electromagnetic compatibility)
reglementation.autorite: European Parliament and Council of the European Union; enforced by national market surveillance authorities
reglementation.citation: Manufacturers shall draw up the technical documentation referred to in Annex II or Annex III and carry out the relevant conformity assessment procedure referred to in Article 14 or have it carried out. Where compliance of apparatus with the applicable requirements has been demonstrated by that procedure, manufacturers shall draw up an EU declaration of conformity and affix the CE marking.
reglementation.exigence: The manufacturer must draw up the EMC technical documentation, carry out the conformity assessment, draw up an EU declaration of conformity and affix the CE marking.
reglementation.note: Listed for the charger only. Article 2(2)(a) of the text as published excludes equipment covered by Directive 1999/5/EC (the former radio equipment directive); for the laptop, EMC is an essential requirement of Directive 2014/53/EU (see eu-red-exigences).

reglementation.titre: Radio equipment essential requirements
reglementation.acte: Directive 2014/53/EU (radio equipment)
reglementation.autorite: European Parliament and Council of the European Union; enforced by national market surveillance authorities
reglementation.citation: Radio equipment shall be constructed so as to ensure: (a) the protection of health and safety of persons and of domestic animals and the protection of property, including the objectives with respect to safety requirements set out in Directive 2014/35/EU, but with no voltage limit applying; (b) an adequate level of electromagnetic compatibility as set out in Directive 2014/30/EU.
reglementation.exigence: The laptop, as radio equipment, must be built to meet the safety objectives of the low voltage directive with no voltage limit and an adequate level of electromagnetic compatibility.
reglementation.note: The laptop contains a Wi-Fi/Bluetooth module, so it is radio equipment. Quoted from the text as originally published; Article 3(1) is unchanged in the consolidated version of 28.12.2024, which was also read. Article 3(2) adds efficient use of radio spectrum. Article 10(3): the manufacturer draws up the technical documentation, carries out the conformity assessment, draws up an EU declaration of conformity and affixes the CE marking; Article 10(4): kept 10 years.

reglementation.titre: USB-C charging port for laptops
reglementation.acte: Directive (EU) 2022/2380 amending Directive 2014/53/EU (common charger)
reglementation.autorite: European Parliament and Council of the European Union; enforced by national market surveillance authorities
reglementation.article: Annex (new Annex Ia to Directive 2014/53/EU), Part I, points 1.13 and 2.1
reglementation.citation: 1.13. laptops. 2. In so far as they are capable of being recharged by means of wired charging, the categories or classes of radio equipment referred to in point 1 of this Part shall: 2.1. be equipped with the USB Type-C receptacle
reglementation.exigence: A laptop that can be recharged by wired charging must be equipped with a USB Type-C receptacle.
reglementation.note: Article 2(1) of Directive (EU) 2022/2380: Member States apply the rules from 28 December 2024 for points 1.1 to 1.12 and from 28 April 2026 for point 1.13 (laptops). The consolidated version of Directive 2014/53/EU dated 28.12.2024 still lists only points 1.1 to 1.12, which is why the amending directive is quoted. Part I point 3 (read in the consolidated text): above 5 V, 3 A or 15 W the equipment must incorporate USB Power Delivery; the laptop label shows a 20 V 3.4 A input. Article 3a: the buyer must be offered the equipment without a charging device, with a pictogram on the packaging and, for distance selling, close to the price. The label does not show the connector type, so the port itself was not checked. This directive regulates the radio equipment, not a charger sold alone.

reglementation.titre: External power supply efficiency limits
reglementation.acte: Commission Regulation (EU) 2019/1782 (ecodesign, external power supplies)
reglementation.autorite: European Commission; enforced by national market surveillance authorities
reglementation.citation: 1. Energy efficiency requirements: (a) from 1 April 2020, the no-load condition power consumption shall not exceed the following values:
reglementation.exigence: The charger must stay within the no-load power consumption limit set in Annex II, which also sets a minimum average active efficiency and nameplate information.
reglementation.note: Scope read in Article 2(1): nameplate output power not exceeding 250 watts, used with the equipment of Annex I (which lists information technology equipment). A 70 W adapter is inside that limit. Values read in Annex II for an AC-DC supply above 49,0 W that is neither low voltage nor multiple voltage output: no-load 0,21 W, average active efficiency not less than 0,880; whether this adapter falls in the low voltage class of Article 2(2) was not determined. This is the regulation in application today: Regulation (EU) 2025/2052 repeals it with effect from 14 December 2028.

reglementation.titre: USB-C interoperable power supplies from 2028
reglementation.acte: Commission Regulation (EU) 2025/2052 (ecodesign, external power supplies and chargers)
reglementation.autorite: European Commission; enforced by national market surveillance authorities
reglementation.citation: An AC-DC EPS shall be an interoperable EPS that meets all the requirements set out in point (b) unless it fulfils the requirements set out in point (c). (b) An interoperable EPS shall satisfy all the following requirements: (1) it shall be fitted with at least one USB Type-C or USB-PD port;
reglementation.exigence: From the date of application, an AC-DC external power supply must be interoperable, which includes at least one USB Type-C or USB-PD port, unless an exemption of point 3(c) applies.
reglementation.note: Not yet in application: Article 10 says the regulation applies from 14 December 2028, and Article 8 repeals Regulation (EU) 2019/1782 from the same date. Article 9(3), applicable from 14 December 2025: a supply placed on the market between 14 December 2025 and 14 December 2028 that meets this regulation is considered to comply with Regulation (EU) 2019/1782. Point 3(c) exempts, among others, supplies with a nameplate output power greater than 100 W; a 70 W adapter is below that limit. The new definition (Article 2(1)) no longer has the 250 W ceiling and covers supplies sold with or without the powered product. Annex III defines a common charger logo.

reglementation.titre: Ecodesign requirements for notebook computers
reglementation.acte: Commission Regulation (EU) No 617/2013 (ecodesign, computers and computer servers)
reglementation.autorite: European Commission; enforced by national market surveillance authorities
reglementation.citation: The ecodesign requirements for computers and computer servers are set out in Annex II. Compliance of computers and computer servers with the applicable ecodesign requirements shall be measured in accordance with the methods set out in Annex III.
reglementation.exigence: The laptop must meet the ecodesign requirements of Annex II, measured with the methods of Annex III.
reglementation.note: Article 1(2)(c) lists notebook computers among the products covered. Dates read in the final article: most points of Annex II apply from 1 July 2014, points 1.2 and 1.4 from 1 January 2016. Text read as originally published; later amendments were not read.

reglementation.titre: Restricted substances file and CE
reglementation.acte: Directive 2011/65/EU (RoHS)
reglementation.autorite: European Parliament and Council of the European Union; enforced by national market surveillance authorities
reglementation.citation: manufacturers draw up the required technical documentation and carry out the internal production control procedure in line with module A of Annex II to Decision No 768/2008/EC or have it carried out; (c) where compliance of EEE with the applicable requirements has been demonstrated by the procedure referred to in point (b), manufacturers draw up an EU declaration of conformity and affix the CE marking on the finished product.
reglementation.exigence: The manufacturer must draw up the technical documentation, carry out internal production control, draw up an EU declaration of conformity and affix the CE marking.
reglementation.note: Article 7(a) requires design and manufacture in accordance with Article 4, which bans the substances of Annex II above the stated concentrations. Annex I category 3 is IT and telecommunications equipment. The original Annex II read here lists six substances (lead, mercury, hexavalent chromium, PBB, PBDE at 0,1 %, cadmium at 0,01 %); the annex has been amended since and the consolidated list was not read in this task.

reglementation.titre: Crossed-out bin symbol on equipment
reglementation.acte: Directive 2012/19/EU (WEEE)
reglementation.autorite: European Parliament and Council of the European Union; enforced by national market surveillance authorities
reglementation.citation: With a view to minimising the disposal of WEEE as unsorted municipal waste and to facilitating its separate collection, Member States shall ensure that producers appropriately mark — preferably in accordance with the European standard EN 50419 ( 25 ) — EEE placed on the market with the symbol shown in Annex IX.
reglementation.exigence: The producer must mark the equipment with the crossed-out wheeled bin symbol of Annex IX.
reglementation.note: The characters ( 25 ) in the quote are the footnote reference of the official text. Annex IX: the symbol must be printed visibly, legibly and indelibly. This is a directive: the obligation is carried by each national transposition, which was not read.

reglementation.titre: Producer registration for distance sellers
reglementation.acte: Directive 2012/19/EU (WEEE)
reglementation.autorite: European Parliament and Council of the European Union; enforced by national market surveillance authorities
reglementation.citation: Producers supplying EEE by means of distance communication as defined in Article 3(1)(f)(iv) shall be registered in the Member State that they sell to. Where such producers are not registered in the Member State that they are selling to, they shall be registered through their authorised representatives as referred to in Article 17(2).
reglementation.exigence: A seller supplying equipment by distance communication must be registered as a producer in each Member State it sells to, directly or through an authorised representative.
reglementation.note: Article 3(1)(f)(iv) defines as producer anyone who sells by distance communication directly to households in a Member State and is established in another Member State or in a third country. Article 12: producers finance collection and treatment of household WEEE. Registers, fees and take-back schemes are national (France, Germany, Italy, Spain, Netherlands each have their own); the national texts were not read.

reglementation.titre: Separate collection symbol on batteries
reglementation.acte: Regulation (EU) 2023/1542 (batteries and waste batteries)
reglementation.autorite: European Parliament and Council of the European Union; enforced by national market surveillance authorities
reglementation.citation: From 18 August 2025, all batteries shall be marked with the symbol for separate collection of batteries (‘separate collection symbol’) as shown in Part B of Annex VI.
reglementation.exigence: The battery inside the laptop must carry the separate collection symbol.
reglementation.note: Article 1(3): the regulation also applies to batteries incorporated into products. The symbol seen is on the laptop label; the battery itself was not photographed. Other points read: Article 38, the battery manufacturer draws up technical documentation, an EU declaration of conformity and affixes the CE marking; Article 13(6), QR code from 18 February 2027; Article 11, portable batteries removable and replaceable by the end-user, applicable from 18 February 2027; Article 55(2), producers must be registered in each Member State where they make batteries available, including batteries incorporated in appliances (Chapter VIII applies from 18 August 2025).

reglementation.titre: Information required in online offers
reglementation.acte: Regulation (EU) 2023/988 (general product safety)
reglementation.autorite: European Parliament and Council of the European Union; enforced by national market surveillance authorities
reglementation.citation: Where economic operators make products available on the market online or through other means of distance sales, the offer of those products shall clearly and visibly indicate at least the following information: (a) name, registered trade name or registered trade mark of the manufacturer, as well as the postal and electronic address at which they can be contacted;
reglementation.exigence: Each online offer must clearly and visibly show the name of the manufacturer and the postal and electronic address at which it can be contacted.
reglementation.note: Article 19(b): where the manufacturer is not established in the Union, the offer must also show the name, postal and electronic address of the responsible person within the meaning of Article 16(1) of this regulation or Article 4(1) of Regulation (EU) 2019/1020. Points (c) and (d): product identification with a picture, and warnings in a language consumers understand. Scope limit read in Article 2(1): for products covered by Union harmonisation legislation, Chapter III Section 1 (which contains Article 16) does not apply, so the responsible person for these two products comes from Regulation (EU) 2019/1020 (see eu-operateur-responsable); Article 19 sits in Section 2.

reglementation.titre: Economic operator established in the Union
reglementation.acte: Regulation (EU) 2019/1020 (market surveillance and compliance of products)
reglementation.autorite: European Parliament and Council of the European Union; enforced by national market surveillance authorities
reglementation.citation: Notwithstanding any obligations set out in applicable Union harmonisation legislation, a product subject to legislation referred to in paragraph 5 may be placed on the market only if there is an economic operator established in the Union who is responsible for the tasks set out in paragraph 3 in respect of that product.
reglementation.exigence: The seller must have an economic operator established in the Union responsible for the tasks of Article 4(3) before the product is placed on the market.
reglementation.note: Article 4(2): that operator is the EU manufacturer, the importer, an authorised representative with a written mandate, or failing those the fulfilment service provider established in the Union. Article 4(4): its name and contact details including postal address must be on the product, its packaging, the parcel or an accompanying document. Article 4(5) lists the legislation concerned, including Directives 2009/125/EC, 2011/65/EU, 2014/30/EU, 2014/35/EU and 2014/53/EU.

reglementation.titre: Meaning of the CE marking
reglementation.acte: Regulation (EC) No 765/2008 (accreditation and market surveillance, CE marking)
reglementation.autorite: European Parliament and Council of the European Union; enforced by national market surveillance authorities
reglementation.citation: By affixing or having affixed the CE marking, the manufacturer indicates that he takes responsibility for the conformity of the product with all applicable requirements set out in the relevant Community harmonisation legislation providing for its affixing.
reglementation.exigence: The manufacturer who affixes the CE marking takes responsibility for conformity with every requirement of the legislation that provides for it.
reglementation.note: Article 30(1): only the manufacturer or its authorised representative may affix the CE marking. Article 30(5): no marking likely to mislead about the meaning or form of the CE marking. For these products the CE marking is provided for by the acts listed in the other EU entries.

reglementation.titre: Electrical equipment safety objectives
reglementation.acte: The Electrical Equipment (Safety) Regulations 2016 (S.I. 2016/1101)
reglementation.autorite: Secretary of State (UK)
reglementation.citation: Before placing electrical equipment on the market, a manufacturer must ensure that it has been designed and manufactured in accordance with the principal elements of the safety objectives.
reglementation.exigence: The manufacturer must ensure the charger is designed and manufactured in accordance with the principal elements of the safety objectives.
reglementation.note: Regulation 3: applies to equipment rated between 50 and 1000 V AC and between 75 and 1500 V DC. Regulation 6(1): declaration of conformity and UK marking before placing on the market. No UKCA mark is in the list of marks seen on the charger; see gb-marquage-ce-reconnu for the CE route. Enforcement body not read in this task.

reglementation.titre: CE marking accepted in Great Britain
reglementation.acte: The Electrical Equipment (Safety) Regulations 2016 (S.I. 2016/1101)
reglementation.autorite: Secretary of State (UK)
reglementation.citation: any reference to “UK marking” is to be read as a reference to the CE marking;
reglementation.exigence: Where the manufacturer uses the EU directive route of regulation 34A, the references to the UK marking in the regulations are read as references to the CE marking.
reglementation.note: Regulation 34A (title: Obligations which are met by complying with obligations in the Directive) extends to England, Wales and Scotland. Paragraph (2) sets the conditions: design to Annex I of the Directive, conformity assessment under Annex III, technical documentation, records in English, CE marking affixed, and an EU declaration of conformity in English. Paragraph (3)(a): regulations 4, 5, 6(1) and (3) are then treated as satisfied. The quote is short because each quote must sit inside one paragraph of the official page. Paragraph (4): the importer must ensure the equipment bears the CE marking. The Radio Equipment Regulations 2017 (regulation 36A) and the Electromagnetic Compatibility Regulations 2016 (regulation 38A) have a provision with the same title in their table of contents; their bodies were not read.

reglementation.titre: Radio equipment essential requirements
reglementation.acte: The Radio Equipment Regulations 2017 (S.I. 2017/1206)
reglementation.autorite: Secretary of State (UK)
reglementation.citation: Before placing radio equipment on the market, a manufacturer must ensure that it has been designed and manufactured in accordance with the essential requirements.
reglementation.exigence: The manufacturer must ensure the laptop, as radio equipment, is designed and manufactured in accordance with the essential requirements.
reglementation.note: Regulation 6(1): the essential requirements include health and safety by reference to the Electrical Equipment (Safety) Regulations 2016 and an adequate level of electromagnetic compatibility. Regulation 10(1): declaration of conformity and UK marking before placing on the market. No USB-C common charger requirement was found in the provisions read for Great Britain.

reglementation.titre: Restricted substances in equipment
reglementation.acte: The Restriction of the Use of Certain Hazardous Substances in Electrical and Electronic Equipment Regulations 2012 (S.I. 2012/3032)
reglementation.autorite: Secretary of State (UK)
reglementation.citation: A manufacturer must not place EEE on the market unless the EEE complies with the requirements of regulation 3 (restriction on the use of certain hazardous substances in EEE).
reglementation.exigence: The manufacturer must not place the equipment on the market unless it respects the substance restrictions of regulation 3.
reglementation.note: Regulation 3 (England, Wales and Scotland version): equipment must not contain the substances listed in Schedule A1 above the maximum concentration values. Regulation 10(2) and regulation 16: technical documentation, declaration of conformity and UK marking. UKCA is in the list of marks seen on the laptop but not on the charger. The contents of Schedule A1 were not read.

reglementation.titre: Crossed out bin symbol in UK
reglementation.acte: The Waste Electrical and Electronic Equipment Regulations 2013 (S.I. 2013/3113)
reglementation.autorite: Secretary of State (UK)
reglementation.citation: Except where paragraph (3) applies, the crossed out wheeled bin symbol [ F2 must ] be affixed in a visible, legible and indelible form to each item of equipment.
reglementation.exigence: Each item of equipment must carry the crossed out wheeled bin symbol in a visible, legible and indelible form.
reglementation.note: The characters [ F2 ... ] in the quote are the amendment marker printed by legislation.gov.uk. Regulation 22(1): the duty falls on the producer or authorised representative who places the equipment on the market. Regulation 14(1A) and (2), also read: a non-UK supplier supplying EEE directly to private households or other users in the United Kingdom must either appoint an authorised representative established in the United Kingdom or be a member of a compliance scheme itself.

reglementation.titre: CE marking optional, declaration required
reglementation.acte: Ordonnance sur les matériels électriques à basse tension (OMBT), RS 734.26
reglementation.autorite: Conseil fédéral suisse; Inspection fédérale des installations à courant fort (ESTI)
reglementation.citation: L’obligation d’apposer le marquage «CE» ne s’applique pas. Si le marquage «CE» est déjà apposé en conformité avec les prescriptions de l’UE sur des matériels selon l’art. 1, al. 1, il n’est pas nécessaire de l’enlever.
reglementation.exigence: The CE marking is not required in Switzerland for low voltage equipment and may stay on the charger if it was affixed in line with EU rules.
reglementation.note: No English version on Fedlex, quote in French. Art. 8 al. 1: any economic operator making the equipment available must be able to present a declaration of conformity; Art. 8 al. 4: in a Swiss official language or in English, and conformity with EU law may be declared under Annex IV of the EU low voltage directive. Art. 4 al. 1: operator obligations follow Articles 6 to 9 of Directive 2014/35/EU. Art. 1: same voltage limits as the EU (50 V to 1000 V AC, 75 V to 1500 V DC). Art. 6 al. 2: if the manufacturer is not in Switzerland, has no representative and there is no importer, the fulfilment service provider must be named on the equipment, packaging or documents.

reglementation.titre: Swiss or CE conformity marking
reglementation.acte: Ordinance on Electromagnetic Compatibility (OEMC), SR 734.5
reglementation.autorite: Swiss Federal Council; Federal Office of Communications (OFCOM)
reglementation.citation: Each apparatus must bear the conformity marking in accordance with Annex 1 point 1 or the foreign conformity marking in accordance with Annex 1 point 2.
reglementation.exigence: The charger must bear either the Swiss conformity marking or the foreign conformity marking of Annex 1 point 2.
reglementation.note: Annex 1 point 2.1: the conformity marking of Annex II to Regulation (EC) No 765/2008 (the CE marking) is permitted. Art. 12: the manufacturer, its authorised representative or, if neither is established in Switzerland, the importer must be able to produce the declaration of conformity and technical documentation for ten years. Art. 4 sets the essential requirements. English translation published by Fedlex, stated there to have no legal force.

reglementation.titre: Conformity marking on radio equipment
reglementation.acte: Ordinance on Telecommunications Installations (TIO), SR 784.101.2
reglementation.autorite: Swiss Federal Council; Federal Office of Communications (OFCOM)
reglementation.citation: All radio equipment must bear the conformity marking in accordance with Annex 1 number 1 or the foreign conformity marking in accordance with Annex 1 number 2.
reglementation.exigence: The laptop must bear either the Swiss conformity marking or the foreign conformity marking of Annex 1 number 2.
reglementation.note: Annex 1 point 2.1: the conformity marking of Annex II to Regulation (EC) No 765/2008 (the CE marking) is permitted. Art. 7 para. 1: safety by reference to the low voltage ordinance with no voltage limit, and electromagnetic compatibility. Art. 7 para. 2bis: radio equipment that can be charged by cable and is widely available must be capable of being charged using a USB-C connection, for the categories defined by OFCOM; the OFCOM provisions were not read, so it is not established here whether laptops are in those categories. English translation published by Fedlex, stated there to have no legal force.

reglementation.titre: Restricted substances in equipment
reglementation.acte: Chemical Risk Reduction Ordinance (ORRChem), SR 814.81, Annex 2.18
reglementation.autorite: Swiss Federal Council; Federal Office for the Environment (FOEN)
reglementation.citation: Without prejudice to Numbers 3 and 8, the manufacturer placing electrical and electronic equipment on the market must ensure that it has been designed and manufactured in accordance with the requirements specified in Number 2.
reglementation.exigence: The manufacturer must ensure the equipment is designed and manufactured within the substance limits of Annex 2.18 number 2.
reglementation.note: Number 2 para. 1 lists ten substances with maximum concentrations in homogeneous material: lead, mercury, hexavalent chromium, PBB, PBDE, DEHP, BBP, DBP and DIBP at 0.1 %, cadmium at 0.01 %. Number 4.1 para. 2: technical documentation and internal production control. Annex 2.15 of the same ordinance covers batteries: number 4.1 requires separate collection information on batteries, including for manufacturers of appliances containing batteries. Version in force on 16 July 2026. English translation published by Fedlex, stated there to have no legal force.

reglementation.titre: External power supply efficiency (Switzerland)
reglementation.acte: Ordonnance sur les exigences relatives à l’efficacité énergétique (OEEE), RS 730.02, annexe 2.2
reglementation.autorite: Conseil fédéral suisse; Office fédéral de l’énergie (OFEN)
reglementation.citation: Les sources d’alimentation visées au ch. 1 peuvent être mises en circulation ou fournies si elles satisfont aux exigences visées à l’art. 3 et à l’annexe II du règlement (UE) 2019/1782.
reglementation.exigence: The charger may be placed on the Swiss market only if it meets Article 3 and Annex II of Regulation (EU) 2019/1782.
reglementation.note: No English version on Fedlex, quote in French. Annexe 2.2 ch. 1.1 and 1.3: scope and definitions are those of Regulation (EU) 2019/1782, so the 250 W limit of the EU text applies. Version of the ordinance in force on 24 July 2026; it still refers to Regulation (EU) 2019/1782. The authority named for enforcement was not read in the text.

reglementation.titre: Computer energy efficiency (Switzerland)
reglementation.acte: Ordonnance sur les exigences relatives à l’efficacité énergétique (OEEE), RS 730.02, annexe 2.3
reglementation.autorite: Conseil fédéral suisse; Office fédéral de l’énergie (OFEN)
reglementation.citation: Les ordinateurs visés au ch. 1 peuvent être mis en circulation ou fournis s’ils remplissent les exigences fixées à l’art. 3 et à l’annexe II du règlement (UE) n o 617/2013 pour le type d’appareil correspondant.
reglementation.exigence: The laptop may be placed on the Swiss market only if it meets Article 3 and Annex II of Regulation (EU) No 617/2013 for its type.
reglementation.note: No English version on Fedlex, quote in French. Annexe 2.3 ch. 1.1: covers the computers listed in Article 1(2) of Regulation (EU) No 617/2013, which includes notebook computers. The authority named for enforcement was not read in the text.

reglementation.titre: FCC authorization before marketing digital devices
reglementation.autorite: Federal Communications Commission (FCC)
reglementation.citation: unintentional radiators shall be authorized prior to the initiation of marketing, pursuant to the procedures for certification or Supplier's Declaration of Conformity (SDoC) given in subpart J of part 2 of this chapter
reglementation.exigence: Before marketing either product in the United States, the seller must hold an FCC equipment authorization for it as an unintentional radiator, by certification or by Supplier's Declaration of Conformity.
reglementation.note: Table 1 of the same paragraph lists 'Class B personal computers and peripherals' and 'Class B external switching power supplies' with 'SDoC or Certification'. § 15.19(a)(3) of the same part requires a compliance statement on the device and § 2.1077(a)(3) says the responsible party for an SDoC must be located within the United States, which matters for a brand established abroad. FCC appears in the laptop marks, not in the charger marks.

reglementation.titre: FCC certification of the radio transmitter
reglementation.autorite: Federal Communications Commission (FCC)
reglementation.citation: all intentional radiators operating under the provisions of this part shall be certified by the Telecommunication Certification Bodies pursuant to the procedures in subpart J of part 2 of this chapter prior to marketing.
reglementation.exigence: The Wi-Fi and Bluetooth transmitter inside the laptop must be certified by a Telecommunication Certification Body before the laptop is marketed.
reglementation.note: The label shows 'FCC ID: RAS-MT7920', the identifier of the module. § 15.212(a)(1)(vi)(A) says that when the module's FCC identification number is not visible once installed, the outside of the host device must display a label referring to the enclosed module, for example 'Contains FCC ID'. The paragraph quoted starts with exemptions (paragraph (c) and § 15.23) that do not concern this product type.

reglementation.titre: DOE efficiency standard for external power supplies
reglementation.autorite: U.S. Department of Energy (DOE)
reglementation.citation: all direct operation external power supplies manufactured on or after February 10, 2016, shall meet the following standards
reglementation.exigence: A direct operation external power supply manufactured on or after February 10, 2016 must meet the DOE energy conservation standards set out in the table of that paragraph.
reglementation.note: The sentence begins 'Except as provided in paragraphs (w)(5), (w)(6), and (w)(7)'. The numeric limits sit in a table that the official renderer serves as an image, so the values and power ranges were not read here. § 430.2 defines a direct operation external power supply as one that can operate a consumer product that is not a battery charger without the assistance of a battery. The classification of this USB PD charger (direct operation, adaptive) must be confirmed by the manufacturer. The date is a date of manufacture. § 429.12(a) also requires the manufacturer to submit a certification report to DOE before distributing a basic model in commerce.

reglementation.titre: Efficiency level marking on the power supply
reglementation.autorite: U.S. Department of Energy (DOE)
reglementation.citation: Any external power supply subject to the standards in paragraph (w)(1) of this section shall be clearly and permanently marked in accordance with the International Efficiency Marking Protocol for External Power Supplies
reglementation.exigence: An external power supply subject to the DOE standards must carry a clear and permanent marking that follows the International Efficiency Marking Protocol for External Power Supplies.
reglementation.note: The table in the same section names the standards of paragraph (w)(1)(ii) 'Level VI'. The marking protocol itself is incorporated by reference and was not opened here.

reglementation.titre: California appliance efficiency certification by manufacturer
reglementation.acte: California Public Resources Code, Section 25402
reglementation.autorite: California Legislature; California Energy Commission (CEC)
reglementation.citation: A new appliance manufactured on or after the effective date of the standards or other cost-effective measures shall not be sold or offered for sale in the state, unless it is certified by the manufacturer of the appliance to be in compliance with the standards or other cost-effective measures.
reglementation.exigence: A new appliance covered by a California efficiency standard may be sold or offered for sale in California only if its manufacturer has certified that it complies with that standard.
reglementation.note: State of California only. The same paragraph says 'sold or offered for sale in the state' covers internet and mail order sales for end use in the state, regardless of the seller's physical location. This statute does not itself name computers: the product scope sits in California Code of Regulations, Title 20, sections 1601 to 1609, whose official site refused the download (see gaps). A CEC compliance advisory of April 8, 2021 read on energy.ca.gov states that those sections contain standards, certification requirements and marking requirements for computers. The 'CEC ID' printed on the laptop label could not be traced to a text read here.

reglementation.titre: Country of origin marking on imports
reglementation.acte: 19 CFR 134.11 (section 304, Tariff Act of 1930, 19 U.S.C. 1304)
reglementation.autorite: U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP)
reglementation.citation: requires that every article of foreign origin (or its container) imported into the United States shall be marked in a conspicuous place as legibly, indelibly, and permanently as the nature of the article (or container) will permit, in such manner as to indicate to an ultimate purchaser in the United States the English name of the country of origin of the article
reglementation.exigence: Each imported product, or its container, must be marked conspicuously, legibly, indelibly and permanently with the English name of its country of origin.
reglementation.note: The sentence opens with 'Unless excepted by law'. 'Made in China' is reported on both labels in the product description, it is not part of the list of conformity marks.

reglementation.titre: No duty-free de minimis entry
reglementation.acte: Executive Order 14388 of February 20, 2026, revising section 2 of Executive Order 14324 of July 30, 2025
reglementation.autorite: President of the United States; enforced by U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP)
reglementation.article: Sec. 2, revised section 2(a) of Executive Order 14324
reglementation.citation: Accordingly, all such shipments, except those sent through the international postal network, shall be subject to all applicable duties, taxes, fees, exactions, and charges.
reglementation.exigence: A low-value shipment that is not sent through the international postal network no longer enters duty free and bears all applicable duties, taxes, fees, exactions and charges.
reglementation.note: The preceding sentence of the order says the duty-free de minimis exemption under 19 U.S.C. 1321(a)(2)(C) shall not apply to any shipment regardless of value, country of origin, mode of transportation, or method of entry (articles covered by 50 U.S.C. 1702(b) aside). The same section requires entry to be filed with an appropriate entry type in the Automated Commercial Environment by a party qualified to make entry. Postal shipments follow section 3 of the order. The date is the one from which the modifications apply to goods entered for consumption, the suspension itself began under Executive Order 14324.

reglementation.titre: Lithium battery must pass UN 38.3
reglementation.autorite: Pipeline and Hazardous Materials Safety Administration (PHMSA), U.S. Department of Transportation
reglementation.citation: Each lithium cell or battery must be of the type proven to meet the criteria in part III, sub-section 38.3 of the UN Manual of Tests and Criteria
reglementation.exigence: The lithium-ion battery inside the laptop must be of a type proven to meet the tests of sub-section 38.3 of the UN Manual of Tests and Criteria.
reglementation.note: The charger has no battery. Paragraph (c) of the same section gives exceptions for smaller batteries (lithium ion battery not exceeding 100 Wh, with the Watt-hour rating marked on the outside case) and paragraph (c)(3) governs the lithium battery mark on packages. The battery's Wh rating is not on the label description, so the applicable packing regime was not determined. § 171.22 authorizes transport in accordance with the ICAO Technical Instructions under conditions.

reglementation.titre: Compliance with Canadian radio technical standards
reglementation.acte: Radiocommunication Act (R.S.C., 1985, c. R-2)
reglementation.autorite: Parliament of Canada; Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada (ISED)
reglementation.citation: No person shall manufacture, import, distribute, lease, offer for sale or sell any radio apparatus, interference-causing equipment or radio-sensitive equipment for which technical standards have been established under paragraph 6(1)(a), unless the apparatus or equipment complies with those standards.
reglementation.exigence: Nobody may import, offer for sale or sell in Canada radio apparatus or interference-causing equipment covered by ISED technical standards unless it complies with those standards.
reglementation.note: Subsection 4(2) adds that equipment for which a technical acceptance certificate is required may only be imported or sold in accordance with that certificate. For the charger, ICES-003 issue 7 section 1.2.3 says an external switched mode power supply marketed separately is under the scope of ICES-001 and may instead be authorized under ICES-003 if intended exclusively for devices within its scope. ICES-001 was not opened here.

reglementation.titre: ISED certification and Radio Equipment List
reglementation.acte: RSS-Gen, Issue 6, General Requirements for Compliance of Radio Apparatus
reglementation.autorite: Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada (ISED)
reglementation.citation: No person shall manufacture, import, distribute, lease, offer for sale, or sell Category I radio apparatus in Canada unless this apparatus is listed on the REL.
reglementation.exigence: Category I radio apparatus may be imported, offered for sale or sold in Canada only if it is certified and listed on ISED's Radio Equipment List.
reglementation.note: Issue 6 is dated July 30, 2026 (Amendment 1, September 15, 2026) and is in force from its publication, with a transition period ending one year after publication during which issue 5 or issue 6 is accepted. That the MT7920 Wi-Fi and Bluetooth module is Category I comes from the applicable RSS, not opened here: the 'IC: 7542A-MT7920' number on the label is a certification number in the format defined in section 9.4.4. The next sentence of 3.4.1 allows manufacture, import and distribution before listing when ISED has approved a deferred listing date.

reglementation.titre: Host label showing the module IC number
reglementation.acte: RSS-Gen, Issue 6, General Requirements for Compliance of Radio Apparatus
reglementation.autorite: Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada (ISED)
reglementation.citation: The host product shall be properly labelled to identify the incorporated modules.
reglementation.exigence: The laptop, as host of a certified radio module, must be labelled so that the incorporated module is identified.
reglementation.note: The section gives two ways for each module: its ISED certification number stays clearly visible when installed, or the host displays that number preceded by the word 'contains', 'contient' or 'contains/contient'. Section 9.4.4 requires the certification number to be preceded by 'IC:'. Whether the label wording on this laptop uses 'Contains' was not checked. Same transition period as the entry above.

reglementation.titre: ICES-003 emission limits for IT equipment
reglementation.acte: ICES-003, Issue 7, Information Technology Equipment (including Digital Apparatus)
reglementation.autorite: Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada (ISED)
reglementation.citation: all products subject to this standard that continue to be manufactured, imported, distributed, leased, offered for sale, or sold in Canada shall comply with issue 7 of ICES-003.
reglementation.exigence: A laptop imported, offered for sale or sold in Canada must comply with ICES-003 issue 7.
reglementation.note: The sentence refers to the end of a one-year transition period that ended on October 15, 2021. Section 4.2 sends labelling to ICES-Gen and gives 'CAN ICES-003(*) / NMB-003(*)' as an example label. ICES-Gen issue 2 section 6.3 requires each unit to bear a label that represents the supplier's declaration of conformity. An external power supply marketed together with the laptop is tested with it and its own label is optional (section 1.2.2).

reglementation.titre: Energy efficiency standard for imported power supplies
reglementation.acte: Energy Efficiency Act (S.C. 1992, c. 36), with Energy Efficiency Regulations, 2016 (SOR/2016-311), sections 586 to 589
reglementation.autorite: Parliament of Canada; Natural Resources Canada
reglementation.citation: No dealer shall, for the purpose of sale or lease, ship an energy-using product from one province to another province, or import an energy-using product into Canada, unless
reglementation.exigence: A dealer may import an energy-using product into Canada for sale only if the product complies with the energy efficiency standard and is labelled as the regulations require.
reglementation.note: The conditions that follow 'unless' are (a) the product complies with the energy efficiency standard and (b) the product or its package is labelled in accordance with the regulations, if any. Section 587(1) of the Regulations prescribes an external power supply as an energy-using product, and for units made on or after July 1, 2017 the exclusion of adaptive external power supplies no longer applies. Section 588 sets the standards (direct operation: CSA C381.1-17, Table D.1). Section 4(4) of the Regulations waives the verification mark when the unit carries the US DOE International Efficiency Marking Protocol mark, a certification body has verified the energy performance information, and the model number matches. 'Dealer' means a person engaged in the business of importing, manufacturing or selling such products: whether a foreign online seller shipping to a consumer is the dealer was not settled here. Section 5 of the Act requires dealers to report prescribed information to the Minister.

reglementation.titre: Electrical safety certification mark (British Columbia)
reglementation.acte: Electrical Safety Regulation, B.C. Reg. 100/2004
reglementation.autorite: Province of British Columbia (Technical Safety BC)
reglementation.citation: a person must not use electrical equipment in British Columbia, or offer for sale, sell, display or otherwise dispose of electrical equipment for use in British Columbia, unless the electrical equipment displays a label or mark as follows:
reglementation.exigence: Electrical equipment may be offered for sale or sold for use in British Columbia only if it displays a certification mark or one of the other labels or marks listed in the section.
reglementation.note: Provincial rule, one province only: electrical product safety is not set by a single federal text and the other provinces were not checked (Ontario's official site is rendered by script and could not be read). The list that follows is (a) a certification mark, (b) a label or mark of an acceptable certification agency, (c) an approval mark, (d) a label for used manufactured homes. Subsection (3) exempts equipment that does not require approval under the B.C. Electrical Code. Whether the cULus mark seen on both labels is a 'certification mark' as defined by the regulation was not checked.

reglementation.titre: Dangerous goods by air follow ICAO
reglementation.acte: Transportation of Dangerous Goods Regulations (SOR/2001-286), Part 12
reglementation.autorite: Transport Canada
reglementation.citation: a person who imports, offers for transport, handles or transports dangerous goods by aircraft must do so in accordance with the requirements of the ICAO Technical Instructions.
reglementation.exigence: Whoever imports or offers for transport by aircraft a laptop containing a lithium-ion battery must follow the ICAO Technical Instructions.
reglementation.note: The sentence opens with 'Unless otherwise provided in this Part'. The Regulations list UN3481, lithium ion batteries contained in equipment, among the lithium battery entries and require the cell or battery type to meet subsection 38.3 of Part III of the Manual of Tests and Criteria. The ICAO Technical Instructions are not a free official text and were not opened. The charger has no battery.

reglementation.titre: NOM-001 safety conformity for power supplies
reglementation.acte: NOM-001-SCFI-2018, Aparatos electrónicos-Requisitos de seguridad y métodos de prueba
reglementation.autorite: Secretaría de Economía
reglementation.article: Capítulo 6, Procedimiento para la evaluación de la conformidad
reglementation.citation: deben demostrar su cumplimiento de acuerdo al PEC descrito en esta misma Norma Oficial Mexicana.
reglementation.exigence: Electronic equipment within the scope of this standard that is imported, marketed or offered by catalogue or internet in Mexico must demonstrate compliance through the conformity assessment procedure of the standard.
reglementation.note: Scope read in section 1.2: the standard also applies to external power supplies sold individually for information technology equipment covered by NOM-019-SCFI-1998, and excludes external power supplies above 250 W. The conformity procedure leads to a certificate of conformity issued by an accredited and approved product certification body. The charger shows NOM-NYCE. Page is the official gazette system (SIDOF) copy of DOF note 5572453.

reglementation.titre: NOM-019 safety of data processing equipment
reglementation.acte: NOM-019-SCFI-1998, Seguridad de equipo de procesamiento de datos
reglementation.autorite: Secretaría de Economía (formerly Secretaría de Comercio y Fomento Industrial)
reglementation.citation: Esta Norma Oficial Mexicana establece los requisitos de seguridad que deben cumplir todos los equipos de procesamiento de datos periféricos o equipos relacionados, que se comercialicen en el territorio de los Estados Unidos Mexicanos.
reglementation.exigence: Data processing equipment marketed in Mexico must meet the safety requirements of this standard.
reglementation.note: Section 1.1(a) names portable machines (laptop, notebook, palmtop) and adds two characteristics written in 1998 (single processor, listed bus technologies), so the fit with a current notebook should be confirmed with a Mexican certification body. The text says it enters into force 60 calendar days after publication. NOM-019-SE-2021, meant to cancel this standard, appears in a regulatory review list of January 2022 but its final publication was not found, so this 1998 text is the one quoted. The certificate requirement and the NOM mark come from other texts not opened here. NOM is not in the laptop marks list.

reglementation.titre: NOM-029 efficiency certificate for power supplies
reglementation.acte: NOM-029-ENER-2017, Eficiencia energética de fuentes de alimentación externa. Límites, métodos de prueba, marcado y etiquetado
reglementation.autorite: Secretaría de Energía, Comisión Nacional para el Uso Eficiente de la Energía (CONUEE)
reglementation.citation: Todo producto comprendido en el campo de aplicación de esta NOM que se importe, fabrique, comercialice, así como los que se distribuyan o suministren con fines promocionales dentro del territorio nacional, debe contar con certificado de conformidad de producto de acuerdo con esta NOM.
reglementation.exigence: An external power supply within the scope of this standard that is imported or marketed in Mexico must hold a product certificate of conformity under the standard.
reglementation.note: Scope: external power supplies that convert AC line voltage to a single fixed DC output voltage at a time, with maximum output power of 250,0 W or less, sold individually or with an end product. A definition covers units with built-in mechanisms that select an output voltage from a preset menu, tested at the lowest and highest levels, but the fit of a USB PD charger should be confirmed with a certification body. Section 10.1 requires marking the efficiency level V or VI in Roman numerals. The text enters into force 180 calendar days after its publication. Certificates are granted to persons established in Mexico or from countries with a free trade agreement.

reglementation.titre: Homologation of radio equipment in Mexico
reglementation.acte: Ley en Materia de Telecomunicaciones y Radiodifusión
reglementation.autorite: Congreso de la Unión; Comisión Reguladora de Telecomunicaciones (the Instituto Federal de Telecomunicaciones continues during the transition)
reglementation.citation: Los productos, equipos, dispositivos o aparatos destinados a telecomunicaciones o radiodifusión que puedan ser conectados a una red de telecomunicaciones o hacer uso del espectro radioeléctrico deberán homologarse conforme a las normas o disposiciones técnicas aplicables
reglementation.exigence: A product that can connect to a telecommunications network or use the radio spectrum, such as a laptop with Wi-Fi and Bluetooth, must be homologated under the applicable technical standards.
reglementation.note: The same article says the applicant for homologation must have an address in Mexico, which matters for a brand established abroad. The decree says it enters into force the day after its publication in the Diario Oficial and that the Instituto Federal de Telecomunicaciones continues in office until the plenary of the new Commission is formed. The homologation guidelines published by the IFT (DOF note 5639645) were opened but not quoted. No Mexican homologation number is in the laptop marks list.

reglementation.titre: DC power supply is a specified appliance
reglementation.acte: Order for Enforcement of the Electrical Appliances and Materials Safety Act (Cabinet Order No. 324 of 1962)
reglementation.autorite: Cabinet of Japan; Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry (METI)
reglementation.article: Appended Table 1 (Re. Article 1, Article 1-2 and Article 2), item (ix), 4
reglementation.citation: 4. DC power supply units (including those with an AC power source device dual use, limited to those with a rated capacity of not more than 1 kilovolt-ampere, and excluding those for testing wireless communication equipment and those with other special structures) 5 years
reglementation.exigence: The seller must treat the charger as a specified electrical appliance when it is a DC power supply unit with a rated capacity of not more than 1 kilovolt-ampere, because that item is listed in Appended Table 1.
reglementation.note: Article 1-2 of the same Order says specified electrical appliances are those listed in the left-hand columns of Appended Table 1. Item (ix) is limited to AC appliances rated 100 to 300 volts at 50 or 60 hertz; the charger label reads 100-240V 50-60Hz. The 5 years is the period of Article 9(1) of the Act for the certificate. The translation states its last version as Cabinet Order No. 96 of 2012: later amendments were not read.

reglementation.titre: Conformity assessment by a registered body
reglementation.acte: Electrical Appliances and Materials Safety Act (Act No. 234 of 1961)
reglementation.autorite: Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry (METI)
reglementation.citation: the Notifying Supplier shall, before their sale, have them assessed with respect to the following items (hereinafter referred to as a "Conformity Assessment") by an organization registered with the Minister of Economy, Trade and Industry pursuant to the provisions of the following paragraph, and must obtain and retain the certificate set forth in said paragraph
reglementation.exigence: Before sale, the notifying supplier must have the specified electrical appliance assessed by a body registered with METI and must obtain and keep the certificate.
reglementation.note: Applies to specified electrical appliances only (see jp-denan-scope-dc-power-supply). The notifying supplier is the manufacturer or importer that notified its business under Article 3. The same paragraph has a proviso when a certificate for the same product type is already held and still within its period. The translation states its last version as Act No. 122 of 2011.

reglementation.titre: No sale without the PSE labelling
reglementation.acte: Electrical Appliances and Materials Safety Act (Act No. 234 of 1961)
reglementation.autorite: Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry (METI)
reglementation.citation: Any person engaged in manufacturing, importing, or selling Electrical Appliances and Materials must neither sell nor display for the purpose of sale said Electrical Appliances and Materials unless the labeling set forth in Article 10, paragraph (1) is affixed to said Electrical Appliances and Materials.
reglementation.exigence: The seller must not sell or display the charger for sale in Japan unless the labelling of Article 10, paragraph (1) is affixed to it.
reglementation.note: The Act does not use the word PSE; METI calls the Article 10 labelling the PSE labelling on its English page. Article 17(1)(i) of the Regulation for Enforcement (japaneselawtranslation.go.jp, law 3006) requires, for specified appliances, the mark of Appended Table 6, the name of the notifying supplier and the name of the conformity assessment body; the marks are drawings, so the diamond and circle shapes were not read as text and are not asserted here. The letters JET on the label were not checked against the list of registered bodies.

reglementation.titre: Importer must notify its business
reglementation.acte: Electrical Appliances and Materials Safety Act (Act No. 234 of 1961)
reglementation.autorite: Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry (METI)
reglementation.citation: All persons engaged in manufacturing or importing Electrical Appliances and Materials must, within 30 days from the commencement of such business, notify the Minister of Economy, Trade and Industry of the following particulars in accordance with the Electrical Appliance and Material classification specified by Ordinance of the Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry
reglementation.exigence: The person importing the charger into Japan must notify the Minister of Economy, Trade and Industry within 30 days from the commencement of that business.
reglementation.note: The obligations of Articles 8, 9 and 10 attach to this notifying supplier. The METI English page meti.go.jp/english/policy/economy/consumer/pse/index.html, read during this task, states that for imported goods it is the importers who are responsible, that no foreign juridical person may make the Notification of Import Business unless it has completed registration as a foreign company in Japan, and gives AC/DC Power Supply Units as an example of Specified Electrical Appliances (Category A); that page later answered HTTP 202 with an empty body to a plain client, so it is not used as the quoted source. How this applies to parcels shipped direct to consumers from abroad was not read.

reglementation.titre: Radio equipment needs the technical conformity mark
reglementation.acte: Radio Act (Act No. 131 of 1950), Chapter 3 technical standards, as explained by the Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications
reglementation.autorite: Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications (MIC)
reglementation.citation: To prevent interference in the use of radio waves, radio equipment used in Japan must conform to the technical standards listed in Chapter 3 of the Radio Act. (Whether a device conforms to the technical standards can be confirmed via the technical conformity mark (Figure 1).)
reglementation.exigence: The seller must supply a laptop whose Wi-Fi and Bluetooth radio conforms to the technical standards of Chapter 3 of the Radio Act, which is shown by the technical conformity mark.
reglementation.note: In the Radio Act (japaneselawtranslation.go.jp, law 3205) Article 4 requires a licence to establish a radio station, with an exception for low power stations that exclusively use radio equipment with a conformity mark, and Article 38-7(2) lets a dealer in products incorporating marked radio equipment affix the same mark to the product. The MIC leaflet at tele.soumu.go.jp/resource/j/others/wifi/en.pdf states that the 5.2 GHz and 5.3 GHz bands are for indoor use only. The numbers R 217-241406 and T D240049217 were not looked up in the MIC database.

reglementation.titre: VCCI voluntary emission control for members
reglementation.acte: VCCI Council Rules for Voluntary Control Measures (technical requirements VCCI-CISPR 32)
reglementation.autorite: VCCI Council (private voluntary council, not a government body)
reglementation.citation: Under the voluntary control measures by the VCCI Council, the member is obliged to conduct MME (multimedia equipment) testing to verify conformity with emission (interference) standards prior to shipment of a product on the Japan market.
reglementation.exigence: A VCCI member must test its multimedia equipment against the emission standards before shipping it to the Japanese market; the scheme is described by the Council as voluntary control.
reglementation.note: Source is the VCCI Council's own site, not a government site, because the scheme is private; no government text on VCCI was found. The obligation binds members only. The same page says the member must ship the product with the prescribed indication on the equipment and in the instruction manual. No statutory EMC obligation for the laptop in Japan was read.

reglementation.titre: Conformity assessment before import or sale
reglementation.acte: Radio Waves Act (Republic of Korea)
reglementation.autorite: Ministry of Science and ICT; National Radio Research Agency (RRA)
reglementation.citation: Any person who intends to manufacture, sell, or import broadcasting and communications equipment, and machinery which causes electromagnetic interference or is affected by electromagnetic waves (hereinafter referred to as "broadcasting and communications equipment, etc.") shall, with regard to the relevant equipment, obtain certification of conformity under paragraph (2), registration of conformity under paragraphs (3) and (4)
reglementation.exigence: Whoever manufactures, sells or imports the laptop must obtain certification of conformity or registration of conformity for it.
reglementation.note: The quoted sentence continues with a third route, interim certification under paragraph (7). KLRI translation, stated on the site to be for reference only. The technical requirements listed in the paragraph include electromagnetic compatibility (Article 47-3). The RRA page rra.go.kr/en/cas/intro.do lists computing devices and peripherals under registration of compatibility. Which route applies to the MT7920 radio module, and whether the charger alone is in scope, were not read. The word KC does not appear in the quoted paragraph. A local agent duty for overseas manufacturers was reported by secondary sources only and is not asserted.

reglementation.titre: Indicate conformity assessment on equipment and packaging
reglementation.acte: Radio Waves Act (Republic of Korea)
reglementation.autorite: Ministry of Science and ICT; National Radio Research Agency (RRA)
reglementation.citation: he/she shall indicate the fact that he/she has undergone conformity assessment on the relevant equipment and the packaging thereof.
reglementation.exigence: The person who obtained the conformity assessment must indicate that fact on the laptop and on its packaging before selling it, including before posting it for sale on a website.
reglementation.note: The start of the paragraph says the duty arises when that person intends to sell or lease the equipment or display it, including posting on the web-site. The form of the indication (KC mark and identifier such as R-C-MD6-MT7920) is set by subordinate rules that were not read. Marking on the packaging could not be checked from the label photo.

reglementation.titre: Level 3 equipment registered and RCM marked
reglementation.acte: Electrical Equipment Safety System (EESS), Level 3 in-scope electrical equipment; AS/NZS 4417.1
reglementation.autorite: Electrical Regulatory Authorities Council (ERAC), EESS participating state regulators
reglementation.citation: All Level 3 in-scope electrical equipment offered for sale must be registered by a Responsible Supplier with the EESS and be marked with the Regulatory Compliance Mark (RCM) in accordance with AS/NZS 4417.1. Only Responsible Suppliers who are registered can sell in-scope Level 3 equipment.
reglementation.exigence: The charger, if it is Level 3 in-scope equipment, must be registered with the EESS by a registered Responsible Supplier and be marked with the RCM.
reglementation.note: Scope read in the EESS document 'In-scope Equipment Definitions and Risk Levels v4.3' (eess.gov.au PDF): 'Power supply or charger' is ticked at risk level 3, defined as a household type device with an output not exceeding 50V AC or 120V ripple free DC for charging batteries or supplying separate equipment, excluding IT and audio visual equipment that uses the output to also transmit data not associated with a power supply or charger function. The same level 3 page requires a valid Certificate of Conformity from a recognised certifier. EESS applies in participating jurisdictions only. The code SAA-230413-EA on the label was not looked up.

reglementation.titre: Responsible Supplier must be locally established
reglementation.acte: Electrical Equipment Safety System (EESS), Responsible Supplier registration
reglementation.autorite: Electrical Regulatory Authorities Council (ERAC), EESS participating state regulators
reglementation.citation: The Australian or New Zealand based person or company must have a business presence in Australia or New Zealand to become a Registered Responsible Supplier.
reglementation.exigence: The seller needs a person or company with a business presence in Australia or New Zealand to act as Registered Responsible Supplier, since an overseas company cannot register.
reglementation.note: The sentence just before on the same page reads that an overseas based company cannot be registered on the EESS Registration Database. The page defines the importer as the first person or company in Australia or New Zealand in the supply chain, whoever handles customs. How this applies to direct shipments from China to consumers was not read.

reglementation.titre: ACMA supplier steps and compliance label
reglementation.acte: Radiocommunications Act 1992; Radiocommunications Equipment (General) Rules 2021; Radiocommunications Labelling (Electromagnetic Compatibility) Notice 2017
reglementation.autorite: Australian Communications and Media Authority (ACMA)
reglementation.citation: Before you supply a product to the Australian market, make sure you: check the rules to follow show your product complies sign and keep records register as a responsible supplier label your product.
reglementation.exigence: Before supplying the laptop to the Australian market, the supplier must check the applicable rules, show compliance, sign and keep records, register as a responsible supplier and label the product.
reglementation.note: Same page: an importer brings a product into Australia for sale, and 'If you ship a product from an overseas distributor to a customer in Australia, we consider you an importer'; products with only overseas markings cannot automatically be supplied. ACMA's step 5 page says the compliance label is typically the RCM and must be no smaller than 3 millimetres in height. Scope for a laptop is by analogy with ACMA's own example of a TV with Bluetooth and Wi-Fi falling under the EMC Labelling Notice and the General Equipment Rules; the labelling notices themselves were not read. ACMA EMC rules for the charger alone were not checked.

reglementation.titre: External power supply energy standard scope
reglementation.acte: Greenhouse and Energy Minimum Standards (External Power Supplies) Determination 2014, under the Greenhouse and Energy Minimum Standards Act 2012
reglementation.autorite: GEMS Regulator (Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water)
reglementation.article: What products are covered? (refers to section 6 of the Determination)
reglementation.citation: The Determination covers single output external power supply units with a maximum output power of 250 W or 250 volt-amperes (VA), that: are designed to supply power to other appliances have an AC input from mains supply have one extra low voltage output (either AC or DC) that is either at a fixed voltage or a user selectable voltage through a selector switch
reglementation.exigence: The seller must determine whether the charger is a covered single output external power supply, in which case the minimum energy performance standards of the Determination apply to it.
reglementation.note: Important scope limit read on the same page under 'What products are not covered?': devices capable of multiple output voltages that are not user-selected, such as 'quick charge' units that change the output voltage depending on the end-use product. The charger is a USB PD unit with 20.6V, 15V, 9V and 5V outputs, so it may fall outside the Determination; this was not decided here. For covered products the page requires a compliant performance mark and tests at 230 V AC; the level VI mark is on the label. The page states the product is under review. The Determination text on legislation.gov.au was not read.

reglementation.titre: GST on low value imported goods
reglementation.acte: A New Tax System (Goods and Services Tax) Act 1999, low value imported goods rules, as explained by the ATO
reglementation.autorite: Australian Taxation Office (ATO)
reglementation.citation: If you are a non-resident business and you sell goods into Australia with a customs value of A$1,000 or less, GST applies and you will have to collect this from your customer and send the GST to us.
reglementation.exigence: A non-resident seller must collect GST from the customer and remit it to the ATO on goods sold into Australia with a customs value of A$1,000 or less.
reglementation.note: Same page: the customs value is the sale price minus freight and insurance from the place of export; consignments over A$1,000 have GST, customs duty and clearance charges charged to the importer at the border; the seller may need to register for GST. Whether the laptop is under A$1,000 depends on its price, which is not known here. Any GST registration turnover threshold was not read on this page and is not asserted.

reglementation.titre: Supplier Declaration of Conformity required
reglementation.acte: Radiocommunications Act 1989 product compliance framework
reglementation.autorite: Radio Spectrum Management (RSM), Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment
reglementation.article: Step 4: Complete a declaration of conformity for your product
reglementation.citation: To certify that a product meets all compliance requirements, you need to complete a Supplier Declaration of Conformity (SDoC).
reglementation.exigence: The supplier must complete a Supplier Declaration of Conformity for the laptop.
reglementation.note: Same page: an SDoC is needed for all radio products under Level of Conformity 1 and all level 2, 3, A1, A2 and A3 products; it may be signed by a New Zealand based agent of an overseas manufacturer or supplier; products supplied under the Radiocommunications Regulations (Mutual Recognition: Australia) Notice 2008 do not need a New Zealand declaration. The level of conformity of the laptop was not determined. RSM step 6 says a supplier must register for a supplier number and that the rules are the same when websites are used to reach the NZ market.

reglementation.titre: R-NZ or RCM compliance label
reglementation.acte: Radiocommunications Act 1989 product compliance framework, labelling requirements
reglementation.autorite: Radio Spectrum Management (RSM), Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment
reglementation.article: Step 7: Label your products, Using the R-NZ
reglementation.citation: When the product is a radio transmitter in a class where the level of conformity is A1, A2 or A3, you need to use the R-NZ compliance mark, not the RCM.
reglementation.exigence: The supplier must label the laptop with the R-NZ compliance mark if its radio transmitter is in a class with level of conformity A1, A2 or A3.
reglementation.note: Same page: 'You must label any products you intend to sell with a compliance mark before you can supply them to the market'; for radiocommunications and EMC products at level of conformity 1, 2 or 3 the RCM is used; the R-NZ is a New Zealand only label for radio products not harmonised with Australia; the mark or the characters R-NZ must be no smaller than 3mm in height. Which level applies to the laptop was not determined.

reglementation.titre: Commodity inspection before import
reglementation.acte: The Commodity Inspection Act (Taiwan)
reglementation.autorite: Bureau of Standards, Metrology and Inspection (BSMI), Ministry of Economic Affairs
reglementation.citation: No commodities subject to inspection shall be released from the production premises, nor be exported or imported, if they do not conform to inspection requirements.
reglementation.exigence: The products, as commodities subject to inspection, must conform to the inspection requirements before they are imported into Taiwan.
reglementation.note: Article 8 of the same Act: for commodities produced overseas, the obligatory inspection applicant is the importer. Scope read in the BSMI booklet 'Taiwan Commodity Inspection Schemes for Electrical and Electronic Products' version 1.87 (bsmi.gov.tw PDF f1768800988860), Appendix C-2: automatic data processing machines under code 8471.30.00.00.8, battery chargers for computer, communication and consumer electronics and other static converters (AC-DC adaptors) under 8504.40 codes, with Registration of Product Certification modules II and III. Which 8504.40 line fits the charger was not decided. The booklet says the authority only accepts applications from Local Suppliers.

reglementation.titre: Commodity Inspection Mark before supply
reglementation.acte: Taiwan Commodity Inspection Schemes for Electrical and Electronic Products, Information Booklet version 1.87 (under the Commodity Inspection Act and the Regulations Governing the Use of Commodity Inspection Mark)
reglementation.autorite: Bureau of Standards, Metrology and Inspection (BSMI), Ministry of Economic Affairs
reglementation.citation: All regulated commodities must bear the Commodity Inspection Mark before they can be supplied to the Taiwan market. Local Suppliers are responsible for ensuring that their regulated commodities are affixed with the Commodity Inspection Mark in accordance to the regulations stipulated by the Competent Authority
reglementation.exigence: Each product must bear the BSMI Commodity Inspection Mark before it is supplied to the Taiwan market, and the local supplier is responsible for affixing it.
reglementation.note: The laptop label shows BSMI R31018; no BSMI mark is in the list of marks seen on the charger, hence false. Article 12 of the Commodity Inspection Act also requires the obligatory inspection applicant to place the mark on the commodity's body. The booklet is BSMI guidance, last updated 19 January 2026 according to its cover.

reglementation.titre: RoHS presence marking in BSMI identifier
reglementation.acte: CNS 15663 Section 5 'Marking of presence', as applied in the Taiwan Commodity Inspection Schemes for Electrical and Electronic Products, Information Booklet version 1.87
reglementation.autorite: Bureau of Standards, Metrology and Inspection (BSMI), Ministry of Economic Affairs
reglementation.article: Chapter 11 Commodity Inspection Mark, Identification number of product certification for RPC Scheme
reglementation.citation: As for those commodities subject to marking requirements stipulated in CNS 15663, Section 5 “Marking of presence” under the RPC Scheme, the identification number of which shall be included “the presence conditions of the restricted substance” (i.e., RoHS or RoHS(XX,XX)).
reglementation.exigence: For commodities subject to CNS 15663 Section 5, the identification number of the Commodity Inspection Mark must include the presence condition of the restricted substances, shown as RoHS or RoHS(XX,XX).
reglementation.marque: RoHS marking in the BSMI identification number
reglementation.note: The laptop label shows 'R31018 RoHS'; nothing equivalent is in the list of marks seen on the charger, hence false. Same booklet: the restricted substances are Pb, Cd, Hg, Cr+6, PBB and PBDE, and Appendix C-2 lists CNS 15663 Section 5 for automatic data processing machines (8471.30.00.00.8) and for the 8504.40 charger and adaptor lines. CNS 15663 itself was not read.
